description: G5 (core src/editor/layout/composition/yards.ts): each lot dressed by its building's role: a porch deck under every door, widened under the porch posts within reach; the yard's edges (fence, hedge or wall by role) inset in the lot, open at the gate, skipped where the house leaves too little clear ground; the role's dressing in the yard's slots. Authored in core; every threshold has a case just inside and just past it. Plan frame: IR (x, z) metres; a lot's away towards its street, across its quarter turn left.

sources.fixturesFrom: conformance/layout/ground-plan.json (copied byte for byte; the corpus test guards the copy)

sources.ruling: U38 (L3 lot-sizing: village lots grow at their source)
sources.inputsFrom: $LOOPS_HOME/features/state/lot-sizing/round-1/g5-yards.ts: the IR's lots (+256, the corpus plan frame); outlines as the IR's spec boxes, or the B8 pack houses through core's fitBuildingToLot (conformance/layout/building-fit.json's Brightwater inputs, lot and node moved to the IR's)

cases.name: yards: Brightwater Vale's seven lots by role
cases.note: The followed plan's lots, their buildings' roles from the IR archetypes (a farm, a smithy, a bakery, an inn, three homes), the settled footprints and the doors: the pack's houses fill their 10 m lots, so most sides are too tight for an edge, and every door still gets its porch deck.

cases.name: yards: Brightwater Vale on its grown lots (L3), the houses as the IR's boxes
cases.note: U38's lots: each building's box plus 2.5 m a side and 5 m behind, its front on the lot's front. The house as the IR states it (its spec box at its position): every back and both sides clear 1 m, so they are edged by role, and every role's dressing finds its slots; the front has no ground (the house stands on the street line), so it is too tight and the square's facades are not fenced.

cases.name: yards: Brightwater Vale on its grown lots (L3), the pack houses fitted to the whole lot
cases.note: The same lots with B8's pack houses fitted by core's fitBuildingToLot to the whole lot, centred, as core stands them today: the House_03 homes fill their 15 m lots to 0.54 m a side and nothing behind (no edge, no dressing), the bakery keeps its sides but no back yard, and the House_01 and House_Large houses stand 1.5-1.8 m off the lot front, so their fronts are fenced too.

cases.name: role: the building table, longest prefix by whole segments
cases.note: The role of each building archetype: a sub-archetype takes its parent's (farm.barn, residence.small); building.residence_small is not under building.residence (whole segments only) and an unknown building has no prefix, so both take the default role, home; restaurant and tavern are inns.

cases.name: yards: a farm with clear ground on every side
cases.note: A 10 x 12 m lot facing +x with a 6 m house set back: 2 m clear behind and at each side, 4 m in front. A fence 0.3 m inside the lot on all four sides, the front open 3 m at the gate, posts every 2 m from each run's start; the farm's hay, cart and trough in the two back corners and the first side's middle; a porch deck under the door.

cases.name: tight: 0.95 m of clear ground at a side gets no edge
cases.note: The farm's house widened so its +across side leaves 0.95 m to the lot's edge: under the 1 m least yard gap that side is too tight, with no fence and no dressing in its slots.

cases.name: tight: 1.05 m of clear ground at a side is edged
cases.note: The farm's house widened so its +across side leaves 1.05 m to the lot's edge: over it, that side keeps its fence and its slots.

cases.name: porch: a post 2.85 m from the door is under the deck
cases.note: A porch post 0.9 m out and 2.7042 m along the wall from the farm's door, 2.85 m off: within the 3 m post reach the deck widens to run 0.3 m past it.

cases.name: porch: a post 3.15 m from the door is loose
cases.note: A porch post 0.9 m out and 3.0187 m along the wall from the farm's door, 3.15 m off: past the reach no door claims it; the deck keeps its least size and the post is reported loose.

cases.name: porch: two posts either side of a door, a deck under both
cases.note: Two posts 1.6 m out and 1.5 m either side of a door facing -z: the deck runs 1.9 m deep and 1.8 m a side, centred on the door's line.

cases.name: yards: a home with no footprint, turned, and an inn whose front is too narrow for a gate run
cases.note: A home's lot facing -z with no measured footprint (all its ground clear): a hedge on four sides and its washing line and planter in the back corners. An inn on a 2.4 m wide lot: the 3 m gate takes the whole front, so it has no front run; a wall on its back and sides.

cases.name: yards: a house over its whole lot
cases.note: A house larger than its lot on every side: every side too tight, no edge, no dressing (all unplaced), and its porch deck still laid.

cases.name: slots: a slot under the house is not used, though its side clears a lower least gap
cases.note: Under a least yard gap of 0.5 m (ruleOverrides), the farm's across+ side has 0.7 m of clear ground and is edged, but its middle slot, 1 m in from the lot's edge, is under the house: it is skipped and the trough takes the other side's middle.

cases.name: porch: a post goes to its nearest door, a post equally near two doors to the lower id; posts answered by id
cases.note: Doors a (0, 0) and b (4, 0), listed b first, both facing -z. Post p1 at (1.5, -1) is 1.80 m from a and 2.69 m from b, both within the 3 m reach: it is a's, its nearest, not the first door listed that reaches it. Post p2 at (2, -1) is 2.24 m from each: the lower id, a, takes it. b's deck has no post. The posts are listed p2 first and two loose posts q2 first: a deck's posts and the loose posts are answered by id.

cases.name: porch: a post on the door's right widens the deck as one on its left does
cases.note: One post 0.9 m out and 2 m to the right of a door facing +x (2.19 m off, within reach): the deck's half width runs 0.3 m past it, to 2.3 m, as it would for a post on the left.

cases.name: edges: a run a whole number of spacings long ends in one post, not two
cases.note: A farm lot 10.6 m across and 12.6 m deep: inset 0.3 m, its back run is 10 m and its side runs 12 m, whole numbers of the 2 m post spacing, so each has a post every 2 m from its start and the post at its end is the last of them (6 on the back, 7 on each side), not a second one on top of it.

cases.name: tight: exactly 1 m of clear ground at a side is edged
cases.note: As the 1.05 m case with the house 1 m from the lot's across+ side: the least yard gap itself is enough, so that side is edged.

cases.name: edges: a front just wider than the gate gets a short run either side of it
cases.note: A farm lot 4.2 m across: inset 0.3 m, its front edge is 3.6 m, 0.3 m wider than the 3 m gate gap each side, so a 0.3 m run stands either side of the gate (a front no wider than the gate gets none).
